subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` as a public model contract with a DeepSeek automatic default, or keep this provider policy internal and config-free?
rationale: Both approaches can address the regression, but only maintainers can decide whether the long-term escape hatch and custom-provider applicability justify expanding the public compatibility/config surface.

options.title: Adopt the scoped compat contract
options.body: Accept this PR's DeepSeek-only automatic default and explicit override after current-head checks and a DeepSeek tool-turn smoke proof; this is recommended because it has complete transport coverage and live cache counters.

options.title: Keep the policy internal
options.body: Retain DeepSeek-specific suffix relocation but remove the public configuration key and related catalog/schema surface before merge.

options.title: Pause for the config-free sibling
options.body: Defer this PR while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94945 is brought to full transport parity and supplied with positive live provider proof.

recommendation.title: Adopt the scoped compat contract
recommendation.body: Accept this PR's DeepSeek-only automatic default and explicit override after current-head checks and a DeepSeek tool-turn smoke proof; this is recommended because it has complete transport coverage and live cache counters.
